correctness.rationale: Ferroni Proposition 2.2 gives exactly the vertex set of a rank-corank reflection-isometric pyramid over \(\Delta_{k-1}\times\Delta_{r-1}\). The reverse convex-hull inclusion uses nonnegative coefficients y_i z_j/s and the origin weight 1-s, also at the boundary s=0. All n coordinate inequalities and the base constraint are facets for k,r>=2. The intrinsic normal projections have lengths h=√((n-1)/n) and b=√(kr/n). For an inscribed radius ρ, the facet offsets impose coordinates >=hρ and common group sum s<=1-bρ. Since s>=max(k,r)hρ, the exact upper bound is ρ<=1/(max(k,r)h+b). Explicit feasible centers attain it. Equality forces the larger coordinate group to equal hρ coordinatewise, and all smaller-group nonnegative surplus vectors sum to (max-min)hρ. This is the entire regular-simplex incenter set, with claimed distances, tangency and sharp n-parametric dimension. Replayed checker solves 121 independently specified Chebyshev linear programs for 2<=k,r<=12, corroborating the proof but not replacing it. All parameters and balanced/low-dimensional boundaries checked.

value.rationale: The connected minimal matroids are uniquely extremal in basis count at each (rank, size), and their canonical base polytopes are natural matroid-geometry objects. The result completely classifies maximum Euclidean inscribed balls for an infinite two-parameter family, including all optimal centers, precise simplex dimensions/edge length and the exact tangent-facet profile. The center set is nonunique in every unbalanced rank-corank class, can have unbounded dimension at fixed near-balanced parameters, and collapses sharply at balance. This metric phase and exact classification are useful geometric data not obtainable from an Ehrhart polynomial or generic affine order-polytope equivalence; the closed form is structurally motivated rather than arbitrary finite enumeration.
